7 WORKPLACE DESIGN

chunks.title:
Primary Function
Labels should describe the function of equipment items
chunks.text:
7.5.3-1 Primary Function
Labels should describe the function of equipment items.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: If needed for clarity, engineering characteristics or nomenclature may also be described.0700

chunks.title:
Wording of Instruction Labels
The label should briefly and simply express the intended action
chunks.text:
7.5.3-2 Wording of Instruction Labels
The label should briefly and simply express the intended action.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Words on labels should be concise and still convey the intended meaning. Brevity should not be stressed
if the results will be unfamiliar to operating personnel Instructions should be clear and direct.

chunks.title:
Commonly Used Terms and Symbols
Terms, abbreviations, and symbols used on panel labels should have commonly accepted meanings for all
intended users
chunks.text:
7.5.3-3 Commonly Used Terms and Symbols
Terms, abbreviations, and symbols used on panel labels should have commonly accepted meanings for all
intended users.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Unusual technical terms should be avoided. Use of Roman numerals should be avoided. Words should
be spelled correctly. Abstract symbols should be used only if they have a commonly accepted meaning (e.g., %).0700

chunks.title:
Distinguishability
Symbols should be unique and distinguishable from each other
chunks.text:
7.5.3-4 Distinguishability
Symbols should be unique and distinguishable from each other.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: A commonly accepted standard configuration should be used.0700

chunks.title:
Consistency
Labels should be consistent within and across panels in their use of words, acronyms, abbreviations, and
part/system numbers
chunks.text:
7.5.3-5 Consistency
Labels should be consistent within and across panels in their use of words, acronyms, abbreviations, and
part/system numbers.0700

chunks.title:
Agreement with Procedures
There should be no mismatch between nomenclature used in procedures and that printed on the labels
chunks.text:
7.5.3-6 Agreement with Procedures
There should be no mismatch between nomenclature used in procedures and that printed on the labels.0700

chunks.title:
Administrative Control
A list of standard names, acronyms, abbreviations, and part/system numbers should be in place and
administratively controlled
chunks.text:
7.5.3-7 Administrative Control
A list of standard names, acronyms, abbreviations, and part/system numbers should be in place and
administratively controlled.0700

chunks.title:
Label Similarity
Words and abbreviations of similar appearance should be avoided where an error in interpretation could result
chunks.text:
7.5.3-8 Label Similarity
Words and abbreviations of similar appearance should be avoided where an error in interpretation could result.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: When labels containing similar words, abbreviations, or acronyms are located in close proximity to each
other, different words should be selected or means of coding should be used to reduce the probability of selecting the wrong control or reading
the wrong display.0700

chunks.title:
Functional Relationship
Labels should be used to identify functionally grouped controls or displays
chunks.text:
7.5.3-9 Functional Relationship
Labels should be used to identify functionally grouped controls or displays.0700
Part 2: HFE Guidelines 399 NUREG-0700, Rev. 1, Vol. 1

--- [NUREG-0700 Page 429] ---
7 WORKPLACE DESIGN

chunks.title:
Label Location
Labels should be located above the functional groups they identify
chunks.text:
7.5.3-10 Label Location
Labels should be located above the functional groups they identify.0700

chunks.title:
Control Position Labels
All discrete functional control positions should be identified
chunks.text:
7.5.3-11 Control Position Labels
All discrete functional control positions should be identified.0700

chunks.title:
Direction
Direction of motion (increase, decrease) should be identified for continuous motion rotary controls
chunks.text:
7.5.3-12 Direction
Direction of motion (increase, decrease) should be identified for continuous motion rotary controls.0700

chunks.title:
Visibility
Control position information should be visible to the operator during operation of the control
chunks.text:
7.5.3-13 Visibility
Control position information should be visible to the operator during operation of the control.0700

chunks.title:
Access Opening Labeling
Each access opening used by control room operators should be labeled to identify the function of items accessible
through it
chunks.text:
7.5.3-14 Access Opening Labeling
Each access opening used by control room operators should be labeled to identify the function of items accessible
through it.0700

chunks.title:
Danger, Warning, and Safety Instruction Labels

chunks.title:
Character Height
Character height should subtend a visual angle of 15 minutes (the viewing distance multiplied by 0
chunks.text:
7.5.6-1 Character Height
Character height should subtend a visual angle of 15 minutes (the viewing distance multiplied by 0.004) as a
minimum; a visual angle of 20 minutes (the viewing distance multiplied by 0.006) is preferred.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Letter height should be identical for all labels within the same hierarchical level, based on the maximum
,. 0700
viewing distance.

chunks.title:
Contrast
Colors should be chosen for maximum contrast against the label background
chunks.text:
7.5.6-2 Contrast
Colors should be chosen for maximum contrast against the label background.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Table 7.7 rates various color combinations in terms of relative legibility. To ensure adequate contrast and
prevent loss of readability because of dirt, dark characters should be provided on a light background. If colored print is used for coding
purposes, it should conform to the established color coding scheme for the control room (see Section 1.3.8).

chunks.title:
Character Selection
Labels should be prepared in capital letters with letters and numerals without flourishes or serifs
chunks.text:
7.5.6-3 Character Selection
Labels should be prepared in capital letters with letters and numerals without flourishes or serifs.0700

chunks.title:
Character Width
Letter width-to-height ratio should be between 1:1 and 3:5
chunks.text:
7.5.6-4 Character Width
Letter width-to-height ratio should be between 1:1 and 3:5. Numeral width-to-height ratio should be 3:5 except
for the numeral "4," which should be one stroke width wider, and the numeral "1," which should be one stroke
in width.0700

chunks.title:
Stroke Width
Stroke width-to-character height ratio should be between 1:6 and 1:8
chunks.text:
7.5.6-5 Stroke Width
Stroke width-to-character height ratio should be between 1:6 and 1:8.0700

chunks.title:
Spacing
The minimum space between characters should be one stroke width
chunks.text:
7.5.6-6 Spacing
The minimum space between characters should be one stroke width. The minimum space between words should
be one character width. The minimum space between lines should be one-half of the character height.0700
Part 2: HFE Guidelines 403 NUREG-0700, Rev. 1, Vol. 1

chunks.title:
Labeling of Equipment
Labels should appear on all components and systems with which operators may
chunks.text:
8.1.1-1 Labeling of Equipment
Labels should appear on all components and systems with which operators may.6146

chunks.title:
Replacement of Labels
When labels are affixed, earlier markings (such as labels applied during construction or acceptance, or informal
labels) should be removed
chunks.text:
8.1.1-2 Replacement of Labels
When labels are affixed, earlier markings (such as labels applied during construction or acceptance, or informal
labels) should be removed.6146

chunks.title:
Viewing Direction
When equipment may be approached from more than one direction, labels should be placed on surfaces so that
they are visible from each direction
chunks.text:
8.1.1-3 Viewing Direction
When equipment may be approached from more than one direction, labels should be placed on surfaces so that
they are visible from each direction.6146

chunks.title:
Label Visibility
Identifying labels should be placed so that they are readily visible at typical viewing distances and orientations
chunks.text:
8.1.1-4 Label Visibility
Identifying labels should be placed so that they are readily visible at typical viewing distances and orientations.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Labels should be placed so as to be visible to plant personnel of both short and tall stature.6146

chunks.title:
Locator Labels
Readily visible markings should be placed nearby to indicate the location and identity of components that are
partially blocked from view
chunks.text:
8.1.1-5 Locator Labels
Readily visible markings should be placed nearby to indicate the location and identity of components that are
partially blocked from view.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The location of overhead valves can be indicated by labels on floors or walls directly below them.6146

chunks.title:
Label Orientation
Labels should be designed and mounted so that text is oriented horizontally for ease of reading
chunks.text:
8.1.1-6 Label Orientation
Labels should be designed and mounted so that text is oriented horizontally for ease of reading.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Requiring operators to manipulate and re-orient the label is inconvenient (especially when their hands are
full), and may lead to misreading.6146

chunks.title:
Label Positioning
Labels should be attached or positioned so as to unambiguously indicate the item being identified
chunks.text:
8.1.1-7 Label Positioning
Labels should be attached or positioned so as to unambiguously indicate the item being identified.6146

chunks.title:
Redundant Labels
When labels are placed on the doors of equipment cabinets, redundant labels should be placed inside so that they
are visible when the door is open
chunks.text:
8.1.1-8 Redundant Labels
When labels are placed on the doors of equipment cabinets, redundant labels should be placed inside so that they
are visible when the door is open.6146

chunks.title:
Label Placement Conventions
Specific conventions for label placement should be employed for each type of equipment (e
chunks.text:

8 LOCAL CONTROL STATIONS

chunks.title:
Label Mounting
Tags should be attached to components so as not to cause damage or interfere withoperation
chunks.text:
8.1.1-10 Label Mounting
Tags should be attached to components so as not to cause damage or interfere withoperation.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Valve labels should not be connected to handwheels or operating chains. The wire used to attach a label
to a valve should be passed through the yoke in a manner that will not damage the stem. For chain-operated valves, the label should be wired
to a small piece of plastic pipe through which the operating chain passes freely. J

chunks.title:
Label Replacement after Maintenance
Maintenance procedures should require personnel to check that labels are in place after components are
reassembled or replaced
chunks.text:
8.1.1-11 Label Replacement after Maintenance
Maintenance procedures should require personnel to check that labels are in place after components are
reassembled or replaced.6146

chunks.title:
Means of Label Attachment
Labels and tags should be securely attached in a manner appropriate to the equipment and environmental
conditions
chunks.text:
8.1.1-12 Means of Label Attachment
Labels and tags should be securely attached in a manner appropriate to the equipment and environmental
conditions.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The method chosen to attach a label should take into account the possibility of exposure to heat, corrosive
substances, oil, or solvents.
NUREG-0700, Rev. 1, Vol. 1 406 Part 2: HFE Guidelines

8 LOCAL CONTROL STATIONS

chunks.title:
Label Material
The material from which labels and tags are made should be appropriate to the equipment and environmental
conditions
chunks.text:
8.1.2-1 Label Material
The material from which labels and tags are made should be appropriate to the equipment and environmental
conditions.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The material chosen should take into account the possibility of exposure to heat, corrosive substances,
oil, or solvents. A single label material may not be appropriate in all environments. If different label material is required at different locations
in the plant, an effort should be made to keep the content and format of the labels constant6146

chunks.title:
Label Contrast
Lettering and background colors should provide high contrast and high legibility
chunks.text:
8.1.2-2 Label Contrast
Lettering and background colors should provide high contrast and high legibility.
ADDrriONAL INFORMATION: Dark letters on a light background are preferred. Table 7.7 provides examples of color combinations and
their relative legibility. Stamped metal tags (brass, stainless steel, and color anodized aluminum) often are illegible under less-than-optimal
conditions.6146

chunks.title:
Character Height
Characters used on labels should be sized to take into account viewing distances and illumination conditions
chunks.text:
8.1.2-3 Character Height
Characters used on labels should be sized to take into account viewing distances and illumination conditions.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The character height recommendations in Guideline 7.5.6-1 should be observed. Character heights
required for various viewing distances are given in Table 8.1. Under less-than-optimal viewing conditions, the preferred values should be used
as minimums. The preferred values should also be used for critical markings associated with safety-related systems.6146

chunks.title:
Stenciled Labels
Stenciled labels should not be used
chunks.text:
8.1.2-4 Stenciled Labels
Stenciled labels should not be used.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The gaps in stenciled characters render them less legible than other forms of labeling.6146

chunks.title:
Label Reflectance
Surfaces of labels should have a non-reflective (i
chunks.text:
8.1.2-5 Label Reflectance
Surfaces of labels should have a non-reflective (i.e., matte) finish.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Reflective materials may be added to labels to aid locating equipment when normal lighting is lost. Such
labels should be designed so that legibility is not impaired under normal lighting conditions; e.g., a reflective border may be placed around
the contents of the label.6146
Part 2: HFE Guidelines 407 NUREG-0700, Rev. 1, Vol. 1

chunks.title:
Label Information
Labels should contain concise, descriptive noun names along with alphanumeric system and component
identification codes
chunks.text:

Labels should contain concise, descriptive noun names along with alphanumeric system and component
identification codes.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Labels should provide sufficient descriptive information to allow the least experienced operator to
recognize the equipment The following additional items may be considered for inclusion on labels: unit/train/channel designations, power
supply information, operational characteristics, and flow direction. 146

chunks.title:
Labeling Conventions

procedures

procedures.6146

Standard Label Format

chunks.text:

chunks.title:
Alignment Marks
Alignment marks should be used to indicate open and closed status of important manual valves
chunks.text:
8.2.3-1 Alignment Marks
Alignment marks should be used to indicate open and closed status of important manual valves.6146

chunks.title:
Visibility of Position Indication
The location and size of the alignment marks should reflect the normal viewing distance, location, and ambient
lighting
chunks.text:
8.2.3-2 Visibility of Position Indication
The location and size of the alignment marks should reflect the normal viewing distance, location, and ambient
lighting.6146

chunks.title:
Indication of Full Open/Closed Positions
Alignment marks should show both the valve
chunks.text:
8.2.3-3 Indication of Full Open/Closed Positions
Alignment marks should show both the valve's fully open and fully closed positions.6146

chunks.title:
Design of Position Indication
Alignment marks should be located to minimize parallax error
chunks.text:
8.2.3-4 Design of Position Indication
Alignment marks should be located to minimize parallax error.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Parallax refers to the apparent change in the relative positions of objects depending on the position of the
viewer, firor will be minimized if the distance between the indicator and the marks against which it is to be read is small, and if the indicator
is located so that it can be viewed "straight-on," i.e., with the observer's LOS perpendicular to the plane of the alignment marks. 146

chunks.title:
Indication of Direction of Rotation
The direction of rotation for opening and closing of a valve control wheel should be indicated in cases where the
direction is not obvious
chunks.text:
8.2.3-5 Indication of Direction of Rotation
The direction of rotation for opening and closing of a valve control wheel should be indicated in cases where the
direction is not obvious.6146

chunks.title:
Precision of Indication
Alignment marks should be precise enough that the observers can tell when a valve is fully opened or closed
chunks.text:
8.2.3-6 Precision of Indication
Alignment marks should be precise enough that the observers can tell when a valve is fully opened or closed.6146

chunks.title:
Alternate Means of Local Position Indication

appropriate
chunks.text:

appropriate.6146

Design of Controls

chunks.text:
8.3.1-1 Design of Controls
The design and operation of controls should conform to the guidance in Section 3.6146

chunks.title:
Inadvertent Activation
Controls should be protected against inadvertent actuation
chunks.text:
8.3.1-2 Inadvertent Activation
Controls should be protected against inadvertent actuation.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: See Guideline 3.1.1-4. The danger of inadvertent actuation of controls may be greater outside the control
room due to ongoing construction, maintenance, calibration, and outage-related activities. Controls can be affected by personnel or equipment
moving by, radio transmissions, or vibration.0700

chunks.title:
Suitability for Operator Use
The operation of controls should be compatible with the use of protective clothing, if it may be required
chunks.text:
8.3.1-3 Suitability for Operator Use
The operation of controls should be compatible with the use of protective clothing, if it may be required.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: See Guideline 3.1.1-12. The likelihood of operators requiring protection (e.g., against heat or radiation)
is greater outside the control room.0700

Loudspeaker coverage should be such that members of the work force can be alerted under all plant conditions.6146

Coverage Areas of Loudspeakers
Loudspeaker coverage should be provided in all areas where the work force may be

chunks.text:
8.4.1-3 Locations and Amplitudes of Loudspeakers
Speakers should be placed within a space so that their number, location, and volume provide an intelligible signal
to all workers therein.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Room size and configuration, and ambient noise levels should be taken into account.6146

Echoes

chunks.text:

or areas near sensitive equipment.

Radio Repeaters
Radio repeaters should be installed to eliminate

Communications training should be provided as a cost effective method of improving efficiency and reliability
of communications.6146

chunks.title:
Periodic Surveillance Programs
Administrative programs should provide for periodic system surveillance
chunks.text:
8.4.5-2 Periodic Surveillance Programs
Administrative programs should provide for periodic system surveillance.6146

chunks.title:
Intelligibility Tests
Determinations of speech intelligibility should be conducted for activities involving critical communications
chunks.text:
8.4.5-3 Intelligibility Tests
Determinations of speech intelligibility should be conducted for activities involving critical communications.6146

chunks.title:
Page System Capacity Upgrading
Multiplexing should be added where needed to expand the number of page-party channels
chunks.text:
8.4.5-4 Page System Capacity Upgrading
Multiplexing should be added where needed to expand the number of page-party channels.6146
Part 2: HFE Guidelines 419 NUREG-0700, Rev. 1, Vol. 1

--- [NUREG-0700 Page 449] ---
8 LOCAL CONTROL STATIONS

chunks.title:
Outdoor Equipment
Equipment located outdoors should be sheltered from the elements as much as possible
chunks.text:
8.5.1-1 Outdoor Equipment
Equipment located outdoors should be sheltered from the elements as much as possible.6146

chunks.title:
Heat Stress
The level of physical activity and required protective clothing, as well as temperature and humidity, should be
considered when assessing the danger of heat exposure posed to operators
chunks.text:
8.5.1-2 Heat Stress
The level of physical activity and required protective clothing, as well as temperature and humidity, should be
considered when assessing the danger of heat exposure posed to operators.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Important considerations are the amount of metabolic heat being generated by the operator and the
restriction of evaporative heat loss associated with protective clothing.6146

chunks.title:
Engineering Controls
Engineering controls should be applied where heat may impair the effectiveness or threaten the well-being of
operators
chunks.text:
8.5.1-3 Engineering Controls
Engineering controls should be applied where heat may impair the effectiveness or threaten the well-being of
operators.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Examples of engineering controls include: shielding or insulating sources of radiant heat, eliminating steam
leaks, increasing ventilation, and providing assists to reduce the strenuousness of the task.

chunks.title:
Work Practices
Work practices should be adopted to minimize risk due to heat exposure which cannot be eliminated by
engineering controls
chunks.text:
8.5.1-4 Work Practices
Work practices should be adopted to minimize risk due to heat exposure which cannot be eliminated by
engineering controls.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Recommended work practices include training in the recognition and treatment of heat illnesses, water and
salt replacement, acclimation, and work/rest cycles (stay times). Illustrations of how temperature (wet-bulb globe temperature, WBGT),
metabolism, and clothing relate to stay times are found in Table 8.2 and Table 8.3.6146

chunks.title:
Water Replacement
Water should be readily available in areas where the potential for heat stress exists
chunks.text:
8.5.1-5 Water Replacement
Water should be readily available in areas where the potential for heat stress exists.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Unusual measures may be necessary to provide drink to workers in restricted areas.6146
NUREG-0700, Rev. l.Vol. 1 420 Part2: HFE Guidelines

chunks.title:
Hearing Protection
Ear protection devices should be available and required to be wom in areas where noise levels are 85 dB or
more
chunks.text:
8.5.2-1 Hearing Protection
Ear protection devices should be available and required to be wom in areas where noise levels are 85 dB or
more.6146

chunks.title:
Sound Attenuating Enclosures
When operators may be required to remain in high noise areas for extended periods of time, appropriate sound
attenuating enclosures should be provided
chunks.text:
8.5.2-2 Sound Attenuating Enclosures
When operators may be required to remain in high noise areas for extended periods of time, appropriate sound
attenuating enclosures should be provided.6146

chunks.title:
Auditory Capabilities of Users
The hearing sensitivity of the work force should be monitored
chunks.text:
8.5.2-3 Auditory Capabilities of Users
The hearing sensitivity of the work force should be monitored.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: The needs of those workers with hearing degradation should be taken into account.6146

chunks.title:
Communications and Hearing Protection
Communication equipment in high noise areas should be compatible with ear protection devices
chunks.text:
8.5.2-4 Communications and Hearing Protection
Communication equipment in high noise areas should be compatible with ear protection devices.6146

8 LOCAL CONTROL STATIONS

chunks.title:
Portable Lighting
Easily used, portable lighting devices should be readily available nearby when permanent lighting (normal or
emergency) may be inadequate
chunks.text:
8.5.3-1 Portable Lighting
Easily used, portable lighting devices should be readily available nearby when permanent lighting (normal or
emergency) may be inadequate.6146
NUREG-0700, Rev. l.Vol. 1 424 Part2: HFEGuidelines

8 LOCAL CONTROL STATIONS

chunks.title:
Permanent Means of Access
Permanent means of access to equipment requiring recurrent or emergency operation should be provided when
it is beyond the normal standing reach of operators
chunks.text:
8.5.4-1 Permanent Means of Access
Permanent means of access to equipment requiring recurrent or emergency operation should be provided when
it is beyond the normal standing reach of operators.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Examples of access provisions include work platforms and ladders.6146

chunks.title:
Temporary Means of Access
Temporary or movable access platforms to equipment should be available when the equipment is located beyond
the normal standing reach of operators and permanent access provision is not feasible
chunks.text:
8.5.4-2 Temporary Means of Access
Temporary or movable access platforms to equipment should be available when the equipment is located beyond
the normal standing reach of operators and permanent access provision is not feasible.6146

chunks.title:
Formal Means of Access
Catwalks, ladders, and other formal means should be provided for operators to reach equipment
chunks.text:
8.5.4-3 Formal Means of Access
Catwalks, ladders, and other formal means should be provided for operators to reach equipment.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Operators should not be required to walk along pipes or to use components as "stepping stones" in order
to reach equipment. 14

chunks.title:
Sufficient Clearance
Sufficient clearance should be provided in the vicinity of equipment in contaminated or high temperature areas
to allow operators easy access despite the use of protective garments and associated gear
chunks.text:
8.5.4-4 Sufficient Clearance
Sufficient clearance should be provided in the vicinity of equipment in contaminated or high temperature areas
to allow operators easy access despite the use of protective garments and associated gear.6146

chunks.title:
Impediments to Access
Access to equipment to be operated should not be impeded by structural elements
chunks.text:
8.5.4-5 Impediments to Access
Access to equipment to be operated should not be impeded by structural elements.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Structural elements added to the plant (e.g., seismic reinforcements) should not restrict access to
equipment.6146
